old: In 2026 a US oil blockade after the fall of Venezuela’s government deepened an economic collapse.
new: In 2026 a US oil blockade, imposed after US forces captured Venezuela’s president, deepened an economic collapse.
problem: Venezuela’s government did not fall: after Maduro’s capture in January 2026 his vice president Delcy Rodríguez and his allies kept power as an acting government.

old: Havana confirmed talks with Washington; US officials said they wanted Díaz-Canel to leave power.
new: Havana confirmed talks with Washington; the New York Times reported that US officials wanted Díaz-Canel to leave power, which Secretary of State Rubio called a fake story.
problem: US officials did not say this on the record; it was an anonymously sourced NYT report that Rubio publicly denied, so stating it as fact is one-sided.

problem: The Supreme People’s Assembly revised the constitution in March 2026, so 2019–2023 is no longer the latest major change.

old: It has survived famine, sanctions and three successions;
new: It has survived famine, sanctions and two hereditary successions;
problem: Three generations of Kims means two successions (Kim Il Sung to Kim Jong Il in 1994, Kim Jong Il to Kim Jong Un in 2011), not three.
sources: Standard chronology; the file’s own timeline lists only the 1994 and 2011 successions

old: Survived famine, sanctions and three successions
new: Survived famine, sanctions and two hereditary successions
problem: Same error in the strengths list: there have been two successions, not three.
sources: Standard chronology; the file’s own timeline lists only the 1994 and 2011 successions

problem: 253/47 was the 2020 split; the 2024 election used 254 districts and 46 proportional seats.

old: protest movements (2009, 2019, 2022 “Woman, Life, Freedom”) were crushed.
new: protest movements (2009, 2019, 2022 “Woman, Life, Freedom”, and the 2025–26 nationwide uprising, in which thousands were killed) were crushed.
problem: It leaves out the December 2025–January 2026 uprising, the deadliest crackdown in the Islamic Republic’s history (even the government admitted over 3,000 deaths).

old: Nine provinces with their own governments; the Western Cape has been run by the opposition for years.
new: Nine provinces with their own governments; the Western Cape has been run by the Democratic Alliance since 2009.
problem: Since 2024 the DA is the ANC’s main national coalition partner, so calling it “the opposition” is out of date.

old: Anonymous electoral bonds (2018) were struck down by the Supreme Court in 2024 after disclosures showed large corporate donations, mostly to the ruling party.
new: Anonymous electoral bonds (2018) were struck down by the Supreme Court in February 2024; the disclosures it then ordered showed large corporate donations, with the ruling BJP receiving about half.
problem: The order is reversed: the court ruled on 15 February 2024 and the donor data came out only in March because the court ordered it. Also the BJP got roughly half (about 47%), not most.

old: (appointed peers, 26 Church of England bishops, and hereditary peers, being phased out)
new: (appointed life peers and 26 Church of England bishops; the last hereditary peers were removed in April 2026)
problem: The House of Lords (Hereditary Peers) Act 2026 is now law, and the hereditary peers left when the session ended on 29 April 2026.

old: The domestic intelligence service monitors parties it considers extremist, including parts of the AfD, which is contested in court.
new: The domestic intelligence service monitors parties it considers extremist; it has watched the whole AfD as a suspected extremist case since 2021, and in February 2026 a court blocked its 2025 upgrade to “confirmed extremist” until a full ruling.
problem: The whole AfD, not just parts, is under observation as a suspected case (upheld by the Münster court in 2024), and the 2025 “confirmed extremist” label was suspended by the Cologne court on 26 February 2026.

old: Main parties: CDU/CSU, SPD, AfD, Greens, the Left, FDP and BSW.
new: Parties in the Bundestag since 2025: CDU/CSU, AfD, SPD, Greens and the Left; the FDP and BSW fell below 5% and lost their seats.
problem: The FDP and BSW failed the 5% threshold in February 2025 and have no Bundestag seats; the AfD is now the second-largest party.
sources: Federal Returning Officer (Bundeswahlleiterin), final results of the 23 February 2025 Bundestag election

old: V-Dem and Freedom House classify it as an electoral autocracy
new: V-Dem classifies it as an electoral autocracy and Freedom House rates it Not Free
problem: “Electoral autocracy” is V-Dem’s category; Freedom House uses Free/Partly Free/Not Free and rates Russia Not Free.
sources: Freedom House, Freedom in the World 2025: Russia (Not Free)

old: the federal government becomes a welfare and regulatory state; unions legalized.
new: the federal government becomes a welfare and regulatory state; the Wagner Act (1935) guarantees the right to form unions.
problem: Unions were already legal (since Commonwealth v. Hunt, 1842); the New Deal’s Wagner Act gave them federal protection and collective-bargaining rights.
